correctness.rationale: Domination in a complete multipartite graph is equivalent to meeting at least two parts or taking one entire part. For a selected vertex in occupied part i, the neighbors outside the dominating set are exactly all omitted vertices outside that part, giving the stated linear inequality. The enumerator then follows by independent binomial choices of omitted vertices. For a fixed support, the maximum internal omission total Y is bounded by total capacity, the smallest-part capacity, and the sum of the pairwise capacity inequalities; the three bounds are jointly sufficient by allocating from the common lower bound max(0,Y-K). Exhaustive direct checking through order nine agrees with the characterization, all coefficients, and the minimum formula.

originality.rationale: The initiating k-limited-domination paper gives exact scalar values for complete bipartite graphs but no complete-multipartite result in its searchable full text. The new claim is explicitly restricted to at least three parts and classifies every feasible set, derives every cardinality coefficient, and solves the minimum for each possible support. Searches also covered the equivalent (0,k)-pitchfork terminology. No covering complete-multipartite theorem was found. The closest database item is instead about k-limited packings, a different neighborhood constraint.

value.rationale: The result extends a newly introduced capacity-constrained domination invariant from a known biclique scalar formula to a complete all-set theory for every multipartite graph with at least three parts. The support inequalities give a reusable structural description, the enumerator records the entire feasible-set distribution, and the fixed-support optimization exposes how inactive parts consume the capacity budget. This is materially stronger than another isolated minimum-value computation.
